## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Gaṇapetavatthu* ("A Large Group of Ghosts", Pv 45) is a canonical verse text belonging to the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The narrative describes an encounter between Arahant Moggallāna and a group of ghosts who undergo severe suffering as the kammic retribution for their stinginess in their previous human lives [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations of the text are cataloged on SuttaCentral across four languages [SuttaCentral].

No curated cross-language parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit are listed by SuttaCentral or detected by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, computational text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus identifies significant internal Pali alignments [DharmaNexus]. The text is extensively cited and commented upon in the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares 67 matching segments with the text, notably spanning §2.2–11.3 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, formulaic verse segments in the narrative—predominantly covering §2.2–3.4 and §2.2–6.4—are shared with other accounts within the *Petavatthu*, most prominently the *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31), *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15), *Dhanapālaseṭṭhipetavatthu* (Pv 19), and *Nandāpetivatthu* (Pv 16) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
